_about: Plain-English summary of each weekly update, keyed by the run id in data/state.json (usually the date, e.g. 2026-11-13). Written by the Friday review. 120-220 words, no hype, setbacks included, no medical advice.

weeks.2026-11-13:
A quiet week for trials. No RP trials started recruiting, changed status or posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and no new trials were added. Two existing records were updated: a National Eye Institute study of rod and cone function in retinal disease (recruiting in Maryland) and a small Mahidol University trial in Thailand testing injections of stem-cell-derived vesicles.

In company news, MeiraGTx said it plans to apply for approval of bota-vec, its gene therapy for X-linked RP, in Europe in December and in the US early in 2027. This follows a Phase 3 trial that missed its main goal in 2025, so regulators will have to weigh mixed results. Ocugen licensed OCU400 to Celairis for Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia and still expects its first Phase 3 results in the first quarter of 2027. The Foundation Fighting Blindness added a FAM161A group to its Uni-Rare natural history study.

Nine new papers were found. Most are lab, animal or gene-description studies; one found that people with identical EYS or USH2A gene changes can progress at very different rates. None changes treatment options today.
weeks.2026-11-20: No new results were posted to ClinicalTrials.gov this week, but one trial opened: a wide-field OCT angiography imaging study at IRCCS San Raffaele in Italy is now recruiting. It is a scanning study, not a treatment. Two new treatment trials were registered and are not yet recruiting. GenAns Biotechnology's GA001, a one-time eye injection being tested against a sham injection, is planned as a 12-person Phase 2 trial in China starting in April 2027. A registry in Pakistan will track people given stem cell products as part of routine care; it does not test whether they work. AAVantgarde Bio's Phase 1/2 trial of AAVB-081, a gene therapy for Usher syndrome type 1B (MYO7A), has stopped recruiting. In news, Nanoscope reported that vision gains from its MCO-010 (MOGENRY) injection held for about four years in long-term follow-up of the RESTORE trial, with no serious side effects reported. The FDA decision is still expected in the first half of 2027. Among 14 new papers, a large French study found that changes in two small RNA genes, RNU4-2 and RNU6, explain about 2% of solved dominant RP cases, which may help more families get a genetic answer.
weeks.2026-11-27:
No RP trials started recruiting or posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov this week, and we found no new company or regulatory news on the treatments we follow. Three new treatment trials were registered; none is recruiting yet.

The most notable is AURORA, a Phase 3 trial by Atsena Therapeutics of ATSN-101, a one-time gene therapy injected under the retina for people aged 3 and older with Leber congenital amaurosis caused by changes in both copies of the GUCY2D gene (LCA1). It plans to enroll 30 people, with a start date listed as March 2027. A Phase 2 study in Pennsylvania will compare two eye drops, nepafenac and brinzolamide, for swelling at the center of the retina (cystoid macular edema) in children aged 3 to 12 with inherited retinal disease. Iridium Medical Technology registered an early feasibility study of its HARP4K retinal implant in up to five people with advanced RP or macular degeneration, planned to start in April 2027.

Among 24 new papers, a University of Michigan study found higher levels of anxiety and depression among people with inherited retinal disease, and an Oxford study found poorer sleep in people with RP. Two animal studies tested an experimental compound and a new gene therapy carrier (the second is a preprint); both are early lab work.
